summary.text: A 33-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department with impaired consciousness about four hours after ingesting an estimated 720 mg of lemborexant and 78 mg of eszopiclone, having reportedly consumed alcohol earlier. Her Glasgow Coma Scale score was 11 and Japan Coma Scale score 10; she was hemodynamically stable with equal reactive pupils and no tremor or diaphoresis.

Rapid urine screening was positive for benzodiazepines, the blood count, metabolic panel and liver tests were unremarkable, the osmolar gap was 20.1 mOsm/L and the estimated blood alcohol concentration was 92.7 mg/dL. Retrospective plasma lemborexant levels were 0.144 µg/mL at four hours and 1.410 µg/mL at nine hours post-ingestion.

She was managed with supportive care alone. Her consciousness gradually improved without specific intervention to full recovery, she could ambulate by nine hours post-ingestion, and she was discharged on hospital day two in good condition.

article_limitations: Graphical abstract has no caption or in-text callout; it is described in the visual submission only and its printed values are not added as text facts.
The graphical abstract prints a Glasgow Coma Scale of 15 at nine hours, which the text does not state; chart values estimated from the plotted line or bar are not facts and do not override the text.
Severity of the central nervous system depression is described as mild in the abstract and conclusion and as moderate in the discussion; both are kept as review-only source-conflict facts.
Intent of the overdose is only implied; blister-pack tablet counts are recorded as review-only and not summed into a dose.
Plasma lemborexant was measured at only two time points; the author calls the later level a peak while noting that only two levels were obtained.
Discussion statements about pharmacokinetics, co-ingestant effects and the fatal comparison case are interpretation or other cases and are not patient facts.
